title: Betaine protects salivary glands from radiation injury by inhibiting the STING/TBK1-mediated inflammatory cascade
content:
Abstract
Salivary glands are highly radiosensitive, and their injury during radiotherapy for head and neck cancer severely compromises patients’ quality of life, representing a major dose-limiting factor. To date, no effective strategy is available to prevent or treat this damage. Betaine, a natural methyl donor with established antioxidant property, was investigated for its protective potential and mechanisms in a rat model of radiation-induced salivary gland injury. Results demonstrated that betaine administration significantly preserved glandular architecture, improved salivary flow rate, and reduced glandular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis induced by radiation. Mechanistically, betaine not only mitigated oxidative stress by reducing ROS and 8-OHdG levels while restoring GPx and CAT activity, but also significantly abrogated the radiation-induced phosphorylation of STING and TBK1. This inhibition attenuated the production of the downstream inflammatory cytokines IL-6 and TNF-α. The blockade of this inflammatory cascade subsequently mitigated the glands tissue damage and restored the expression of the functional channel protein AQP5. In conclusion, betaine effectively protects salivary glands from radiation injury by counteracting oxidative stress and suppressing the STING/TBK1-driven inflammatory pathway, offering a promising therapeutic strategy to prevent radiotherapy-induced xerostomia.
